slides.texte_overlay:
Money lessons nobody teaches
young men
Your first salary sets your habits. If you spend it all, you'll keep spending it all. Save a part from the very first month.
Cars are expensive in ways you don't see. Insurance, repairs, parking, fuel. Buy cheaper than you can afford and keep it longer.
Friends spend differently. You don't have to follow the most expensive one. Suggest cheaper plans, good friends will be happy to join.
Your time has value. Before buying something, think about how many hours of work it costs. It changes many decisions. Think in hours, not prices.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Learning is the cheapest upgrade you'll ever make. Start small.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Learning is the cheapest upgrade you'll ever make.

slides.texte_overlay: Debt for things that lose value is a trap. Phones, clothes, holidays on credit. Pay cash for what you can, wait for what you can't.
Ask questions about money. To parents, older friends, colleagues. Most people are happy to share what they learned the hard way.
